name: Notion
look: Deep navy hero band, signature purple pill CTA, pastel feature cards, sober 8px/12px geometry.

hero.title: The workspace that works the way you do
hero.sub: Write, plan and organise in one place. Almanac replaces the four tools your team keeps half-using and never quite abandoning.

features.title: Everything in one place, finally
features.sub: Notes, databases, projects and documentation, sharing one link structure and one permissions model.

items.title: Docs that behave
items.body: A block editor where every paragraph, table and toggle can be moved, linked and referenced from anywhere else.

items.title: Databases, not spreadsheets
items.body: The same records viewed as a table, a board, a calendar or a gallery, with filters that belong to the view.

items.title: Projects with context
items.body: The task and the document that explains it live in the same place, so the spec is never a stale link.

items.title: A wiki people read
items.body: Verified pages, owners and an expiry date, so the handbook stops quietly rotting.

items.title: AI in the page
items.body: Summarise a thread, draft a brief, or ask a question of the whole workspace without leaving the document.

items.title: Permissions that make sense
items.body: Inherited by default, overridable per page, and auditable from a single screen.

showcases.title: One set of records, six ways to look at it
showcases.body: A database in Almanac is a set of records with typed properties. A table, a board, a calendar and a gallery are just saved views over the same rows, so nothing has to be kept in sync.
points: Filters and sorts saved per view
Formulas with a real type system

showcases.title: The handbook that stops rotting
showcases.body: Pages carry an owner and a verification date. When a page goes stale it says so at the top, and the owner gets a nudge rather than the reader getting bad information.
points: Analytics on what people actually read

metric_lead: Across workspaces with more than twenty members

gallery.title: Start from a template
gallery.sub: Thirty-two thousand templates from the community, free to duplicate into your workspace.

testimonial.quote: We cancelled three subscriptions in the first month. The fourth one we kept, and honestly only because one person likes the keyboard shortcuts.
testimonial.name: Rosa Delgado

pricing.title: Plans for every team
pricing.sub: Free for individuals, forever. Paid plans add collaboration, history and controls.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.desc: For individuals organising their own work.

items.q: Is the free plan genuinely free?
items.a: Yes, and permanently. Individuals get unlimited pages and blocks. The paid plans exist for teams that need shared blocks, longer history and administrative controls.

items.q: Can I import from other tools?
items.a: There are importers for the common suspects — documents, wikis, spreadsheets and Markdown archives — and page structure and links are preserved rather than flattened.
You do. Everything can be exported at any time as Markdown, CSV, HTML or PDF, individually or as a full workspace archive.

items.q: How does the AI use our data?
items.a: Workspace content is used to answer your questions and is not used to train shared models. AI can be disabled workspace-wide by an administrator.

cta.title: Get started, free
cta.sub: Join four million teams. No card required, and the free plan does not expire.

footer.tagline: One workspace for your notes, docs, projects and team knowledge.

notes: The navy hero band is the signature opening move, with the product UI card sitting on it under a deep drop shadow.
The purple pill is the primary CTA and appears once per view. Everything else is a text link or a bordered secondary.
Buttons are 8px rounded, cards 12px — deliberately not pills. The geometry is sober and editorial.
Feature cards draw from a pastel set (peach, rose, mint, lavender, sky, yellow) echoing the product's database property colours.
The hero is centred, which sets it apart from the left-aligned norm across B2B SaaS.
